description: The bar chart illustrates the average number of likes received by social media posts, categorized by the angle of the headline’s visual presentation, as defined by five angular intervals: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450]. The vertical axis, labeled “Avg. Like #”, ranges from 400 to 600 in increments of 50, indicating the average number of likes per post. Each bar is a light blue rectangle with a vertical error bar extending above and below, representing variability or confidence intervals. The first bar, corresponding to the (0,90] interval, reaches approximately 600 likes, the highest among all categories. The second bar, (90,180], is slightly lower at around 565 likes. The third bar, (180,270], is approximately 570 likes. The fourth bar, (270,360], is close to 595 likes, and the fifth bar, (360,450], is around 585 likes. The bars are arranged horizontally in order of increasing angle interval, with no clear monotonic trend, suggesting that headline popularity varies non-linearly with angular presentation. The chart does not include a legend, and all bars share the same color and style, with error bars indicating measurement uncertainty. The x-axis labels are rotated slightly for readability. The chart appears to be part of a study on optimizing social media post headlines, as suggested by the paper title “How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media.”
